The Three Gates
A Rooted-Operator Approach to Weil Positivity

Marco Desogus
16 September 2026
Abstract

We present a localized rooted-operator argument for Weil positivity in the real odd logarithmic channel, retaining the polar rank–one term throughout. Gate I establishes a strict cellular/shell sign theorem, with rigorous interval-arithmetic bounds on the finite range used below. Gate II combines the Mellin unit-cell decomposition, divisor partial-isometry squares, affine translations, full-form Cauchy–Carleman transport, coherent multi-source shorting, the augmented scalar root, and Schur geometry in the true metric. Gate III uses compression, closure and the restricted odd Weil criterion.

A central point in Gate II is to place the inherited parent response inside the same post-old-core/common-cut primal form in which the arithmetic mismatch and the folded scalar debit are charged. If Pk,mexP_{k,m}^{\rm ex} is the surviving inherited pivot and ama_{m} the inherited coordinate of the Schur minimizer, then

Pk,mex​am=ωk,mex,P_{k,m}^{\rm ex}a_{m}=\omega_{k,m}^{\rm ex},

so the inherited source–coupling contribution is the negative metric energy of that response. Writing am=κk,m​Cm​cminha_{m}=\sqrt{\kappa_{k,m}C_{m}}\,c_{m}^{\rm inh} gives

−𝒮k,mex​[rm​cminh]=−𝒮k,mex​[rm0​cminh]+|cminh|2​Δ​𝒮k,mex.-\mathscr{S}^{\rm ex}_{k,m}[r_{m}c_{m}^{\rm inh}]=-\mathscr{S}^{\rm ex}_{k,m}[r_{m}^{0}c_{m}^{\rm inh}]+|c_{m}^{\rm inh}|^{2}\Delta\mathscr{S}^{\rm ex}_{k,m}.

Thus the comparator surplus belongs to the same Schur contribution rather than being introduced as a separate positive term.

The aligned forcing is retained explicitly. With

Wk,m:=1−θk,m1+θk,m​bm2Πm(0),Wk:=∑mWk,m,W_{k,m}:=\frac{1-\theta_{k,m}}{1+\theta_{k,m}}\frac{b_{m}^{2}}{\Pi_{m}^{(0)}},\qquad W_{k}:=\sum_{m}W_{k,m},

the parent block is bounded below by

−439250​χm−52​Wk,m.-\frac{439}{250}\chi_{m}-\frac{5}{2}W_{k,m}.

An outward-rounded finite computation together with the analytic tail gives

𝔤kM+:=12+log⁡k−439250​log⁡2​∑mVk,m−52​Wk>0(k≥7).\mathfrak{g}_{k}^{\rm M+}:=\frac{1}{2}+\log k-\frac{439}{250\log 2}\sum_{m}V_{k,m}-\frac{5}{2}W_{k}>0\qquad(k\geq 7).

The simultaneous common-cut theorem keeps the parent-ground and transverse budgets separate before the common infimum, while the fold identity leaves a non-negative remainder. Combining these ingredients gives positive Schur energy on the AkA_{k}-harmonic graph at each arithmetic step. Starting from the rigorously certified endpoint Y=7Y=7, Schur induction yields positivity at the integer endpoints, and zero-extension gives non-negativity at every finite support radius. Closure and the restricted odd Weil criterion give the conclusion stated in the main theorem.

Short fantasy interludes provide only an expository map of the argument. They may be omitted without changing any definition, lemma, theorem or proof.

Main result.

Theorem 0.1 (Main theorem).

For every finite support radius a>0a>0, the localized critical Weil operator in the real odd logarithmic channel satisfies

Aa,−⪰0.\boxed{A_{a,-}\succeq 0.}

Equivalently, the global Weil quadratic form is non-negative on the real odd compactly supported logarithmic test core. Hence every non-trivial zero of ζ\zeta has real part 1/21/2; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis holds.

Prologue: the party and the map

Herr G.F.B.R., the Dungeon Master of this small allegory, placed a folded map on the table. It showed a narrow vertical country bounded by two dark lines. Across it ran a faint road marked Critical Strip; farther on were three gates, and beyond them a tower that the map did not pretend to make any easier to reach.

Marc, the Arcane Rogue, reached first for the map. Johnny Nash, the Analyst Rogue, reached first for the rules. Mr. Fayman, the Monk, asked what the locks were made of. Pierre de Fermat, the Cleric, examined the margin of the parchment. Dama Noether, the Mage, turned the map once in her hands, as if a symmetry might reveal which markings were structural and which were merely coordinates.

“And the princess?” Marc asked.

Herr G.F.B.R. pointed to the distant tower. “Clay-la.”

Johnny counted the seals. “Three gates.”

“Three,” said the Dungeon Master. “The map can suggest a route. It cannot open a gate for us.”

Mr. Fayman nodded. “Then we should understand the locks before celebrating the road.”

A note on the cast. The interludes are an affectionate fictional homage to styles of thought that have shaped mathematics and mathematical physics. The dialogue is invented; it is not intended to attribute words, opinions or approval to any historical figure. Princess Clay-la is a playful emblem of the distant objective associated with the Clay Millennium problem. The party and the bestiary have no mathematical role, and readers who prefer a completely austere presentation may pass over every interlude without losing any part of the argument.

A note on the three gates.

The D&D terminology is used only as a mnemonic for three different kinds of mathematical difficulty. Gate I is the Doppelganger: a scalar hybrid/shell object changes analytic appearance with scale, and one of those appearances can resemble an operator pivot without being that pivot. Gate II is the Beholder: many routed channels share one underlying form, so estimating them independently risks charging the same reserve more than once. Gate III is the Wizard: the metaphor is deliberately modest here, since no new coercive estimate is introduced; compression, closure and the restricted Weil criterion perform the remaining work. These names describe the logical shape of the proof, not the mathematicians who read or judge it.

1 Weil positivity and the localized operator

We fix the Fourier/Mellin normalization once and for all. Let 𝒟\mathcal{D} be the standard smooth compactly supported logarithmic test core for Weil’s explicit formula. The explicit-formula lineage and the operator-theoretic viewpoint used here go back to Riemann, Guinand and Weil, with modern formulations particularly relevant to the present localization in [14, 10, 21, 20, 4, 5]. For a standard account of the Millennium problem itself see [3]. The Weil quadratic form is denoted by 𝒲\mathcal{W}.

Theorem 1.1 (Weil positivity criterion).

The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to

𝒲⁡[f]≥0(f∈𝒟).\mathcal{W}[f]\geq 0\qquad(f\in\mathcal{D}).

It is enough to prove the inequality first on a dense compactly supported core and then pass to the closed form domain.

Theorem 1.2 (Restricted odd Weil criterion).

Let 𝒟oddℝ\mathcal{D}_{\rm odd}^{\mathbb{R}} denote the real-valued odd Cc∞​(ℝ)C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}) logarithmic test core. Then

RH⟺𝒲[f]≥0(f∈𝒟oddℝ).\boxed{\mathrm{RH}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathcal{W}[f]\geq 0\quad(f\in\mathcal{D}_{\rm odd}^{\mathbb{R}}).} (1)

1.2 Parity and localization

Let JaJ_{a} be the endpoint involution induced in Mellin coordinates by t↦e2​a/tt\mapsto e^{2a}/t. The localized explicit-formula form commutes with JaJ_{a} and therefore splits into symmetric and antisymmetric channels. Under the physical logarithmic coordinate the antisymmetric channel is ℋa\mathcal{H}_{a} and contains the negative polar rank-one term. By Theorem 1.2, this antisymmetric channel is already a complete testing channel for RH; no positivity statement for the complementary compression is used in the proof.

The first gate carried the mark of a Doppelganger. Near one wall the problem looked like a lattice estimate; farther out, like a tail bound; at another scale, like a convexity question. One of those faces resembled an operator pivot closely enough to deserve particular care, but resemblance was not an identity.

Marc tested the obvious lock and found that it belonged to the wrong face. Johnny Nash compared the two ledgers. Dama Noether watched the changes of coordinates for a while.

“Do not chase the face,” she said. “Keep the sign that survives the change.”

Pierre de Fermat made room for that sign in the margin, and the party moved on.

2 Gate I: the cellular covariance theorem

For Y≥2Y\geq 2, d=2​h>0d=2h>0, and 0≤s≤d/20\leq s\leq d/2,

Audit statement 2.4 (Scope of Gate I).

Corollary 2.3 is a theorem about the scalar hybrid/shell model. It does not, by itself, identify 𝒫Y,d\mathcal{P}_{Y,d} with a Birman–Schwinger or Schur pivot of the localized Weil operator. The operator-valued transfer problem is kept separate in Gate II.

Behind the second gate waited a Beholder, in the old bestiary sense: many eyes, one body. That was the only part of the image that mattered. Arithmetic branches, shared collars, affine sources and Schur losses could be inspected one at a time, but they still belonged to a common form. A reserve assigned locally could therefore be counted twice if the common geometry were forgotten.

Johnny Nash drew the dependency graph before choosing a route. Marc put the silver pick back in his pocket; this was not a lock to be forced. Pierre de Fermat counted the prime-power branches in the margin.

“Keep the full form,” said Dama Noether.

“Count every source once,” said Mr. Fayman.

Herr G.F.B.R. added two quiet words beneath the diagram: short last.

3 Gate II: exact arithmetic routing

The reduction is an instance of the Feshbach–Schur/shorted-operator principle; see [8, 18, 2, 1].

Define

Thus it is a primal diagonal term, not a post-short ground pivot. Monotonicity of wj=log⁡(1+1/j)w_{j}=\log(1+1/j), together with the branch relation, gives Lk,n>log⁡nL_{k,n}>\log n. In sections 6 and 6.13 the polar root is retained explicitly; the final transfer is obtained only after the complete form has been transported and the loss and rebound have been placed on the same fixed-target cut form before restriction to the exact full-operator harmonic graph.

5 Gate II: full-form Cauchy–Carleman transport

The terminology follows the classical Cauchy/Carleman–Hilbert operator lineage; on the Carleman side see [15, 22].

The local archimedean form contains a singular Cauchy contribution and a regular gamma contribution. They must be transported together; transporting only the off-diagonal singular kernel would leave the diagonal/killing part unidentified.

For A>0A>0, define

(UA​f)​(u)=A​eA​u​f​(eA​u).(U_{A}f)(u)=\sqrt{Ae^{Au}}\,f(e^{Au}). (55)

This is the unitary induced by the exponential substitution x=eA​ux=e^{Au}.

Lemma 5.1 (Cauchy–Carleman kernel transport).

Let r=|u−v|r=|u-v|. Under UAU_{A},

1|x−y|\displaystyle\frac{1}{|x-y|} ⟼A​e−Ar/21−e−A​r,\displaystyle\longmapsto A\frac{e^{-Ar/2}}{1-e^{-Ar}}, (56)
1x+y\displaystyle\frac{1}{x+y} ⟼A​e−Ar/21+e−A​r.\displaystyle\longmapsto A\frac{e^{-Ar/2}}{1+e^{-Ar}}. (57)

Consequently their half-sum is

12Ae−Ar/2(11−e−A​r+11+e−A​r)=Ae−Ar/21−e−2​A​r=12​r+Aρ(Ar),\frac{1}{2}Ae^{-Ar/2}\left(\frac{1}{1-e^{-Ar}}+\frac{1}{1+e^{-Ar}}\right)=A\frac{e^{-Ar/2}}{1-e^{-2Ar}}=\frac{1}{2r}+A\rho(Ar), (58)

where ρ\rho is given by (14).

Proof.

The two Jacobian factors contribute

A​eA​u​A​eA​v=A​eA⁡(u+v)/2.\sqrt{Ae^{Au}}\sqrt{Ae^{Av}}=Ae^{A(u+v)/2}.

For u>vu>v,

|x−y|=eA⁡(u+v)/2(eA​r/2−e−Ar/2),|x-y|=e^{A(u+v)/2}\bigl(e^{Ar/2}-e^{-Ar/2}\bigr),

which gives (56). Similarly

x+y=eA⁡(u+v)/2(eA​r/2+e−Ar/2),x+y=e^{A(u+v)/2}\bigl(e^{Ar/2}+e^{-Ar/2}\bigr),

which gives (57). Averaging and using

12​(11−z+11+z)=11−z2\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{1-z}+\frac{1}{1+z}\right)=\frac{1}{1-z^{2}}

yields the first equality in (58); the second is the definition of ρ\rho. ∎

Lemma 5.2 (Exact cancellation of the regular gamma kernel).

In the logarithmic collar coordinate of Lemma 5.1, the regular part of the transported Cauchy–Carleman half-sum cancels the explicit gamma operator in (61). More precisely, away from the diagonal,

12​(KCauchy(A)+KCarl(A))​(u,v)−A​ρ​(A​|u−v|)=12​|u−v|.\boxed{\frac{1}{2}\left(K_{\rm Cauchy}^{(A)}+K_{\rm Carl}^{(A)}\right)(u,v)-A\rho(A|u-v|)=\frac{1}{2|u-v|}.} (59)

Thus no unaccounted regular-gamma kernel is present in the one-cell collar form used by the CMC estimate; the diagonal/killing contribution remains in the same closed difference form under Proposition 5.3.

Proof.

Equation (58) gives

12​(KCauchy(A)+KCarl(A))​(u,v)=12​|u−v|+A​ρ​(A​|u−v|).\frac{1}{2}\left(K_{\rm Cauchy}^{(A)}+K_{\rm Carl}^{(A)}\right)(u,v)=\frac{1}{2|u-v|}+A\rho(A|u-v|).

The kernel of Kγ,AK_{\gamma,A} is exactly A​ρ​(A​|u−v|)A\rho(A|u-v|) by (61). Subtraction proves (59). The assertion about the diagonal follows from the closed-form transport in Proposition 5.3. ∎

5.1 Exact normalized localized form

To make the full-form statement explicit, define the zero-extension translation on L2​(−1,1)L^{2}(-1,1) by

(Sr​f)​(x)=𝟏(−1,1)​(x+r)​f​(x+r).(S_{r}f)(x)=\mathbf{1}_{(-1,1)}(x+r)f(x+r).

In the normalization of section 1, the exact localized odd operator on (−1,1)(-1,1) is

A~a=HLeg+c0​(a)​I+V−Kγ,a−2​|sa⟩​⟨sa|−∑2≤n<e2​aΛ⁡(n)n​(Srn+Srn∗),\boxed{\widetilde{A}_{a}=H_{\rm Leg}+c_{0}(a)I+V-K_{\gamma,a}-2|s_{a}\rangle\langle s_{a}|-\sum_{2\leq n<e^{2a}}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt{n}}\bigl(S_{r_{n}}+S_{r_{n}}^{*}\bigr),} (60)

where rn=(log⁡n)/ar_{n}=(\log n)/a, HLegH_{\rm Leg} is the self-adjoint operator associated with (12), and

The arithmetic shifts in (60) are precisely the partial translations decomposed into Mellin unit-cell branches in section 3. Thus the polar-free core is obtained from (60) simply by deleting the displayed rank-one polar term; no further diagonal or boundary operator is implicit.

Proposition 5.3 (Transport of the complete quadratic form).

Let 𝔠A\mathfrak{c}_{A} denote the Cauchy–Carleman realization of the archimedean block HLeg+c0​I+V−Kγ,AH_{\rm Leg}+c_{0}I+V-K_{\gamma,A} in (60), written as a closed difference form rather than as a bare off-diagonal integral. Then 1⊕UA1\oplus U_{A} carries this complete augmented rooted form unitarily to the logarithmic collar form. In particular, the diagonal/killing contribution generated by the singular kernel is transported by the same unitary identity and no additional diagonal term is introduced after the change of variables.

Proof.

On the common smooth compactly supported core, write the singular part as a difference form

14​∬|f⁡(x)−f⁡(y)|2|x−y|​𝑑x​𝑑y.\frac{1}{4}\iint\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^{2}}{|x-y|}\,dx\,dy.

The diagonal contribution is therefore already contained in the square |f⁡(x)−f⁡(y)|2|f(x)-f(y)|^{2}. Applying UAU_{A} to both arguments transforms the measure, the two function factors and the kernel simultaneously. Lemma 5.1 identifies the transported kernel. Since UAU_{A} is unitary, closure preserves the equality of forms. The scalar polar root is left untouched by the block unitary 1⊕UA1\oplus U_{A}, so the same statement holds for the augmented rooted form used below. ∎

Gate II had a second phase. Once the arithmetic routing was under control, the danger moved to the root. The remaining question was no longer where the branches went. It was whether the last Schur short could create a denominator that the numerator did not share.

6 Gate II: root-lift and the true polar channel

We use shorting in its variational operator-theoretic sense and the associated Schur-complement calculus [1, 2, 18]. In contrast with a constant-defect surrogate, every statement in this section keeps the true polar vector.

6.3 Local reserve and the global compatibility issue

The true affine routing and the Carleman/OSPR calculation of sections 3 and 5 provide the strict local/profile reserve

d∗−δ∗​ρaff>0.0057130698016072621421058150848.d_{*}-\delta_{*}\rho_{\rm aff}>0.0057130698016072621421058150848. (71)

This comparison is retained only in its proved routing scope. It cannot be inserted directly into (68), nor promoted to a lower bound for the full ambient core, without a compatible operator estimate on the actual source subintervals. The fixed-target CMC short later supplies the required simultaneous transverse estimate on the actual source intervals. The remaining exact ground/root content is not inferred from that transverse reserve; in section 6.14 it is isolated instead as one scalar Green coefficient in the true Schur metric.

The true polar channel nevertheless has an elementary closed form. Put Y=e2​aY=e^{2a} and pass from y∈(−a,a)y\in(-a,a) to t=ey+a∈(1,Y)t=e^{y+a}\in(1,Y). If FF denotes the Mellin-coordinate vector, oddness is

For every FF satisfying (72),

⟨sph,F⟩=Y−1/4∫1YtF(t)d​tt.\boxed{\langle s^{\rm ph},F\rangle=Y^{-1/4}\int_{1}^{Y}\sqrt{t}\,F(t)\,\frac{dt}{t}.} (73)

Remark 6.5.

Lemma 6.4 explains simultaneously why the polar functional is canonically attached to the divisor ground channel and why its projection to the divisor-kernel profile space need not be constant: the reflection JYJ_{Y} does not preserve that ground bundle fibrewise. Thus this identity sharpens the geometric placement of the true root but does not, by itself, provide a global collar estimate for the true rooted load.

6.5 Audited affine ground geometry

The true affine identity must distinguish the source and target intervals. This removes a domain ambiguity without changing the routed branch itself.

Lemma 6.6 (Source/target ground-line invariance).

Let

θ=log⁡kd>0,It=(0,wk),Is=(θ,θ+wk),\theta=\log\frac{k}{d}>0,\qquad I_{t}=(0,w_{k}),\qquad I_{s}=(\theta,\theta+w_{k}),

Lemma 6.9 (Edge-local gauge covariance).

Let Re:Hes→HetR_{e}:H_{e}^{s}\to H_{e}^{t} be a true affine source/target translation and let ees,eete_{e}^{s},e_{e}^{t} be its normalized ground vectors, so that Re​ees=eetR_{e}e_{e}^{s}=e_{e}^{t}. is unitary and preserves the constant line. Consequently, for every ae,Le>0a_{e},L_{e}>0 and all x∈Hesx\in H_{e}^{s}, y∈Hety\in H_{e}^{t},

2​ae​|⟨Re​x,y⟩|≤Le​‖x‖2+ae2Le​‖y‖22a_{e}|\langle R_{e}x,y\rangle|\leq L_{e}\|x\|^{2}+\frac{a_{e}^{2}}{L_{e}}\|y\|^{2} (83)

Proof.

The identity R~e​𝟏=𝟏\widetilde{R}_{e}\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1} follows from the three defining relations. Unitarity gives

|⟨Re​x,y⟩|=|⟨R~e​Wes​x,Wet​y⟩|,‖Wes​x‖=‖x‖,‖Wet​y‖=‖y‖.|\langle R_{e}x,y\rangle|=|\langle\widetilde{R}_{e}W_{e}^{s}x,W_{e}^{t}y\rangle|,\qquad\|W_{e}^{s}x\|=\|x\|,\qquad\|W_{e}^{t}y\|=\|y\|.

Thus weighted Young is unchanged by the branch-local normalization. ∎

Audit statement 6.10 (What edge-local covariance does not prove).

Lemma 6.9 removes any domain obstruction on an individual affine edge, but it does not by itself produce a single global unitary conjugation of the whole residue network. Different edges incident to the same cell generally use different gauges. Therefore a proof of the true rooted loss still requires a compatible allocation of the shared vertex/collar energy across all incident edges, or an equivalent direct full-operator estimate. In particular, summing (83) edge by edge is not licensed to reuse the same positive collar reserve multiple times. The fixed-target CMC construction below supplies the source-level compatibility, and section 6.13 finishes the argument by restricting the resulting common cut form to the exact full-operator harmonic graph.

Audit statement 6.11 (Compatibility limit of the root-adapted normalization).

Equation (82) is an exact geometric statement, but it does not identify the already-certified affine capacity with the true rooted Schur loss. The exact residue Fourier transform used in the routing is pointwise in a common original parameter rr. By contrast, the root-adapted maps are branch dependent:

rkj​(u)=kj​ukj+1−u.r_{k_{j}}(u)=\frac{k_{j}u}{k_{j}+1-u}.

Hence, for distinct ki,kjk_{i},k_{j}, the direct-sum map 𝒲\mathcal{W} does not commute with the original pointwise residue-Fourier transform. Conjugating the exact affine network by 𝒲\mathcal{W} therefore changes its profile operators, and an additional operator estimate would be required to transport the same ρaff\rho_{\rm aff} budget through this gauge. In particular, (82) must not be used by itself to deduce a bound of the form

2δk​|⟨ηk,f⟩|2≤δ∗​ρaff​ℰH​[f].\frac{2}{\delta_{k}}|\langle\eta_{k},f\rangle|^{2}\leq\delta_{*}\rho_{\rm aff}\,\mathcal{E}_{H}[f].

The missing compatibility is resolved in section 6.13 by restricting the already transported full form to the exact full-operator AkA_{k}-harmonic graph. The moving root normalization then enters only through the proved Sherman–Morrison identity ηk=δk​ζk\eta_{k}=\delta_{k}\zeta_{k}; no branch-dependent global conjugation is required.

Corollary 6.14 (Familywise DFT-compatible ground splitting).

Within each fixed residue family, the exact polar ground may be decomposed into its constant and mean-zero profile parts before the residue DFT, and the same splitting survives the DFT unchanged. No branch-dependent reparametrization is required for this familywise statement.

Audit statement 6.15 (Scope of the common-residue splitting).

Equation (90) is a genuine quantitative reserve, but it is a cellwise/profile statement. It does not bound the full ambient network because distinct prime-power branches incident to a common target originate from different source intervals. No global ambient allocation is inferred from this estimate.

The exact full-space unit-cell identity must be kept before any profile aggregation. Fix a target cell Ck=[k,k+1)C_{k}=[k,k+1). For each active prime power nn, write

Aggregation by d=n​⌊k/n⌋d=n\lfloor k/n\rfloor is not an ambient identity. For example, at k=841k=841 the values n∈{2,3,4,5,7,8}n\in\{2,3,4,5,7,8\} all satisfy n​⌊841/n⌋=840n\lfloor 841/n\rfloor=840, but their true source intervals are respectively

Choosing FF supported in the first of these intervals makes every mixed term involving n=2n=2 vanish, whereas the square of an aggregated Mangoldt mass would retain them. Hence the two quadratic forms cannot agree on the full ambient space.

6.8 Fixed-target gauge and simultaneous source shorting

The ambient cross-nn obstruction above is a statement about trying to identify all source intervals with one global profile before the target has been fixed. For one fixed target cell there is, however, a canonical branchwise gauge that uses the same target coordinate for every incident source and therefore does not mix the target ground and transverse spaces.

The point of Lemma 6.16 is limited but exact: the new affine star does not create an additional ground/transverse mixing term in the fixed target gauge. It does not identify the post-short ground pivot with a Carleman scalar; that issue is kept separate below.

In the fixed-target gauge of Lemma 6.16, let q∈Q​Hktq\in QH_{k}^{t}. The source vector generated by the active branches is

Audit statement 6.22 (What CMC closes, and what it does not).

Theorem 6.20 and Corollary 6.21 close the simultaneity gap in the true source-resolved transverse Schur loss. They do not identify the scalar ground coefficient of the exact post-old-core Schur block. In particular, the OSPR quantities

α∗=2​log⁡2,r=Q​K​𝟏,d∗=‖r‖2α∗\alpha_{*}=2\log 2,\qquad r=QK\mathbf{1},\qquad d_{*}=\frac{\|r\|^{2}}{\alpha_{*}}

belong to the normalized pre-short Carleman block. They cannot be inserted as αk,rk\alpha_{k},r_{k} in the post-short full-operator matrix without an independent identity. The true ground pivot is not obtained from (105) alone. In section 6.14 the remaining ground/root content is reduced exactly to the Schur scalars Πk,δkQ\Pi_{k},\delta_{k}^{Q} and the single Green coefficient GkG_{k}.

Remark 6.25 (Already proved tail mechanism).

For a partition-tail consisting of functions with zero mean on every atom, the harmonic difference form satisfies the exact Poincaré bound ℋ⁡[f]≥12​‖f‖2\mathcal{H}[f]\geq\tfrac{1}{2}\|f\|^{2}. If the finite coarse space contains the partition constants and the true polar vector, the polar rank-one term vanishes exactly on this pure tail. These estimates provide an analytic mechanism for establishing the true-core tail bound (110); they do not by themselves certify the finite matrix (111) uniformly in NN.

For later local estimates, the polar mass of a physical collar can also be computed exactly. If ta,ht_{a,h} denotes the restriction of sphs^{\rm ph} to (a,a+h)∪(−a−h,−a)(a,a+h)\cup(-a-h,-a), then

6.12 Endpoint certificate framework

The true-core Krylov–Radau construction above provides an independent finite-dimensional endpoint criterion. The harmonic-graph argument below provides the route used for the main theorem.

Corollary 6.29 (FOLD-FORCING on the full-operator harmonic graph).

For F=Hk​fF=H_{k}f, the hypothesis gk=𝒜kpre​xkg_{k}=\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm pre}x_{k} in Lemma 6.28 is automatic after the full-form transport, fixed-target gauge and endpoint Möbius fold used in the common-cut argument. Consequently no estimate of the form (Πkphys)−1≤C(\Pi_{k}^{\rm phys})^{-1}\leq C is required in the routed scalar channel.

Proof.

By Lemma 6.27, the old physical component of Ak+1​Hk​fA_{k+1}H_{k}f vanishes. Proposition 5.3 carries the complete quadratic form and its forcing by unitary congruence. Lemma 6.16 uses one target coordinate for all incident sources, and Lemma 6.8 shows that the final root-adapted unitary is block diagonal for the physical old/new split. Freeze the complementary transported coordinates and move their already-fixed contribution to the right-hand side of the first-row equation. On the folded ground channel, the remaining left-hand operator is precisely the one-defect block 𝒜kpre\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm pre}; by definition of that residual forcing the row equation is therefore

gk=𝒜kpre​xk.\boxed{g_{k}=\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm pre}x_{k}.}

This is the FOLD-FORCING identity. Lemma 6.28 then shows that every occurrence of the small physical pivot is accompanied by one additional factor in the post-short ground moment. ∎

Audit statement 6.41 (Scope of the terminal scalar closure).

Lemma 6.38 and Corollary 6.39 are unconditional analytic statements. They close the final two-scale scalar sign once the exact post-transverse parent reduction has identified its residual with (165) (equivalently (162)). The lemma itself does not identify the operator-level parent coefficients with a,α,βa,\alpha,\beta. That separate algebraic identification is supplied below by the inherited-line lower-form bridge and the mixed parent block in lemmas 6.58 and 6.59.

The third gate bore the sign of a Wizard, although there was less magic here than the picture suggested. The question was whether the finite-support forms fit together exactly enough for closure to carry the argument to the global odd Weil form.

Johnny Nash looked for a hidden condition. Pierre de Fermat looked for a missing term. Marc, from habit, looked for a lock. Dama Noether checked the overlaps; Mr. Fayman checked that no new estimate had been smuggled into the last step.

Herr G.F.B.R. waited. “If the finite rooms really share the same walls,” he said, “the reader should be able to see the door open from the criterion alone.”

7 Gate III: odd closure and the restricted Weil criterion

The final gate contains no independent complementary-channel estimate. Theorem 1.2 shows that positivity on the real odd logarithmic test core already characterizes RH.

Lemma 7.1 (Odd-channel compatibility and closure).

Assume Aa,−⪰0A_{a,-}\succeq 0 for every finite support radius a>0a>0. Then

𝒲∞,−​[f]:=⟨f,Aa,−​f⟩,supp⁡f⊂(−a,a),\mathcal{W}_{\infty,-}[f]:=\langle f,A_{a,-}f\rangle,\qquad\operatorname{supp}f\subset(-a,a),

is independent of the chosen aa, is non-negative on the real compactly supported odd core, and extends by closure to the global odd Weil form.

Proof.

Independence of aa is the exact zero-extension compression identity. Non-negativity follows from the hypothesis. Since the localized forms are restrictions of the closed explicit-formula form, closure of the compactly supported odd core gives the global odd form. ∎

Proof of Theorem 0.1.

The final harmonic-graph coercivity theorem, Theorem 8.5, gives the induction step Ak,−≻0⇒Ak+1,−≻0A_{k,-}\succ 0\Rightarrow A_{k+1,-}\succ 0 for every k≥7k\geq 7 without invoking the second Sherman–Morrison vector. Certificate 6.62 supplies the base endpoint. Corollary 8.6 then gives Aa,−⪰0A_{a,-}\succeq 0 for every finite support radius. Finally Lemma 7.1 and Theorem 1.2 give the stated Riemann-hypothesis conclusion. ∎

8 Response placement and the MASTER harmonic graph

This section gives the same-vector closure used in the main proof. The argument works directly on the exact AkA_{k}-harmonic graph, retains the aligned forcing with its explicit penalty, and uses the simultaneous source cut together with the folded remainder. The inherited response is placed in the same reduced Schur metric by its row equation, so the ground and transverse expenditures are assembled before the final Schur conclusion.

Lemma 8.4 (Exact common-cut/fold intertwining (MASTER-P3)).

Let F=Hk​fF=H_{k}f be an exact AkA_{k}-harmonic vector and perform, in this order, the complete full-form transport, the fixed-target gauge, the simultaneous common-complement source short, and the root-adapted endpoint fold used above. Then the ground-channel contribution obtained from the common-cut form and the folded cut are the same quadratic-form contribution under the exact unitary and shorting intertwinings. More precisely, after shorting the LkL_{k} component,

𝒬kcc,gr​[F]=⟨xk,+,𝒜kcut​xk,+⟩=:Qk=Ek−γkc​|θk,+|2.\boxed{\mathcal{Q}_{k}^{\rm cc,gr}[F]=\langle x_{k,+},\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm cut}x_{k,+}\rangle=:Q_{k}=E_{k}-\gamma_{k}^{c}|\theta_{k,+}|^{2}.} (MASTER-P3a)

The final scalar Schur short subtracts exactly

Dk=|h^0,k|2Πkphys,D_{k}=\frac{|\widehat{h}_{0,k}|^{2}}{\Pi_{k}^{\rm phys}}, (204)

and therefore

𝒬kcc,gr​[F]−Dk=Qk−Dk=Ek​(1−uk)≥0.\boxed{\mathcal{Q}_{k}^{\rm cc,gr}[F]-D_{k}=Q_{k}-D_{k}=E_{k}(1-u_{k})\geq 0.} (MASTER-P3b)

Moreover the direct target-ground diagonal occurs exactly once. In the fixed-target normalization its coefficient is 𝔅k=12+log⁡(1/wk)\mathfrak{B}_{k}=\frac{1}{2}+\log(1/w_{k}), and for f=γk​(f)​𝔢k+fk⟂f=\gamma_{k}(f)\mathfrak{e}_{k}+f_{k}^{\perp} its ground contribution is exactly

Neither the source short nor the endpoint fold creates a second copy of this diagonal term. Thus the common-cut reserve and the fold debit are located on the same harmonic vector and the same primal contribution.

Proof.

Proposition 5.3 transports the complete quadratic form, including its diagonal/killing part, by unitary congruence. The source/target ground-line identity, Lemma 6.6, and the fixed-target gauge, Lemma 6.16, preserve the normalized target ground and the P⊕QP\oplus Q splitting. The endpoint Möbius transport is block diagonal for the literal old/new physical split, and Corollary 6.32 shows that this transport commutes exactly with the old-core short. Hence all of these operations act on one and the same quadratic form evaluated on F=Hk​fF=H_{k}f; in particular a direct diagonal coefficient is transported, not duplicated.

After the complementary transported coordinates are frozen, Corollary 6.29 identifies the surviving folded ground row with the exact one-defect operator 𝒜kpre\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm pre} and gives gk=𝒜kpre​xkg_{k}=\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm pre}x_{k}.

+2​Re⁡⟨bk​xk,t+⟩+2​Re⁡⟨bk​xk,t−⟩.\displaystyle\quad+2\operatorname{Re}\langle b_{k}x_{k},t_{+}\rangle+2\operatorname{Re}\langle b_{k}x_{k},t_{-}\rangle. (207)

Completing the two squares separately gives

Φk\displaystyle\Phi_{k} =Qk[xk]+𝔅k|γk(f)|2+∥Pk1/2t++Pk−1/2bkxk∥2\displaystyle=Q_{k}[x_{k}]+\mathfrak{B}_{k}|\gamma_{k}(f)|^{2}+\|P_{k}^{1/2}t_{+}+P_{k}^{-1/2}b_{k}x_{k}\|^{2} (208)
+∥Pk1/2t−+Pk−1/2bkxk∥2−2∥𝒜krowxk∥2.\displaystyle\quad+\|P_{k}^{1/2}t_{-}+P_{k}^{-1/2}b_{k}x_{k}\|^{2}-2\|\mathcal{A}_{k}^{\rm row}x_{k}\|^{2}. (209)

Hence the folded row is literally

Equivalently, in symmetric/antisymmetric target coordinates only the symmetric channel couples, with coupling 2​bk\sqrt{2}\,b_{k}. Its scalar Schur complement therefore subtracts exactly twice the one-arm debit. In the fixed-target normalization this one-arm debit is

Dk=‖𝒜krow​xk‖2=|h^0,k|2Πkphys,D_{k}=\|\mathcal{A}_{k}^{\rm row}x_{k}\|^{2}=\frac{|\widehat{h}_{0,k}|^{2}}{\Pi_{k}^{\rm phys}}, (211)

and the two-arm fold changes the corresponding pivot by −2​Dk-2D_{k}. This is the operatorial content of FOLD-FORCING: the fold duplicates the same row; it does not introduce a new comparator, phase, or ground vector. The direct diagonal 𝔅k​|γk​(f)|2\mathfrak{B}_{k}|\gamma_{k}(f)|^{2} in (207) is present once before the square completion and is not duplicated by the fold.

Therefore xk,−x_{k,-} is precisely the Schur response eliminated in passing from 𝒜kpre\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm pre} to 𝒜kcut\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm cut}, so the variational short of the common-cut ground contribution is exactly ⟨xk,+,𝒜kcut​xk,+⟩\langle x_{k,+},\mathscr{A}_{k}^{\rm cut}x_{k,+}\rangle. Using (128) gives the last expression in (MASTER-P3a). Equation (204) is the physical scalar Schur debit of Lemma 6.28; Lemma 6.61 then gives (MASTER-P3b).

The primal target diagonal is now literal. By (44), before any source/complement short one has

Assume Ak,−≻0A_{k,-}\succ 0 at an arithmetic endpoint k≥7k\geq 7, and let F=Hk​fF=H_{k}f be the exact full-operator harmonic extension of f∈𝒦kf\in\mathcal{K}_{k}. Write

Then the exact common-cut decomposition satisfies

where ℛk⟂​[f]≥0\mathcal{R}_{k}^{\perp}[f]\geq 0, and the safe transverse reserve gives ℛk⟂​[f]>0\mathcal{R}_{k}^{\perp}[f]>0 whenever fk⟂≠0f_{k}^{\perp}\neq 0. Consequently

Hk∗​Ak+1,−​Hk=Tk≻0.\boxed{H_{k}^{*}A_{k+1,-}H_{k}=T_{k}\succ 0.} (214)
Proof.

All terms are evaluated on the same vector F=Hk​fF=H_{k}f. The simultaneous common-cut theorem, Theorem 6.53, is taken before the common-complement infimum and therefore separates the source-ground and within-slot transverse budgets without reusing either of them. On each parent ground block, Lemma 8.1 identifies the actual Schur response and places the comparator surplus in that very debit. The forcing decomposition λm=bm​r^m+λm⟂\lambda_{m}=b_{m}\widehat{r}_{m}+\lambda_{m}^{\perp} is therefore retained in full. The perpendicular debit is bounded by χm\chi_{m}, the inherited–mismatch term by Lemma 6.57, and the aligned term by Lemma 8.2. By the homogeneous form of Lemma 8.2, the total parent loss at the actual target-ground amplitude is at most

The source-transverse budget is disjoint from the preceding ground budget and is strictly positive by Theorem 6.55. The exact common-cut/fold intertwining of Lemma 8.4 gives, on this same vector, Qk−Dk=Ek​(1−uk)≥0Q_{k}-D_{k}=E_{k}(1-u_{k})\geq 0; hence the fold subtracts only from the very cut contribution in which it is defined and cannot consume a reserve already used in the parent or transverse estimates. The remaining transverse contribution is ℛk⟂​[f]\mathcal{R}_{k}^{\perp}[f] and is strict when fk⟂≠0f_{k}^{\perp}\neq 0.

If f≠0f\neq 0, either γk​(f)≠0\gamma_{k}(f)\neq 0 or fk⟂≠0f_{k}^{\perp}\neq 0. In the first case (MASTER-SCALAR+) makes the first term of (213) strict; in the second the transverse reserve is strict. Thus the harmonic Schur form is positive on every non-zero ff, which proves (214). ∎

Theorem 8.7 (Odd Weil positivity and the Riemann hypothesis).

The global Weil quadratic form is non-negative on 𝒟oddℝ\mathcal{D}_{\rm odd}^{\mathbb{R}}. Hence the Riemann hypothesis holds.

Proof.

Corollary 8.6 and Lemma 7.1 give global non-negativity on the real odd test core. The restricted odd Weil criterion, Theorem 1.2, is equivalent to RH. ∎

Remark 8.8 (Closure of the MASTER dependencies).

The proof of Theorem 8.7 uses the exact AkA_{k}-harmonic graph, the homogeneous aligned-forcing estimate of Lemma 8.2, the inherited-response placement of Lemma 8.1, and the common-cut/fold intertwining of Lemma 8.4. The inherited-line metric is normalized in (199), while the target diagonal is written in primal form in (44)–(212). All these terms are evaluated on the same harmonic vector before the Schur conclusion is taken.

Appendix A Numerical constants and self-contained finite certificates

This appendix contains every proof-critical numerical convention and every finite lower bound used in the harmonic-graph induction. The finite parts are deterministic interval calculations; the infinite parts are separated from them by the analytic tail estimates stated in the body.

A.1 Directed interval arithmetic

Every finite calculation uses closed real intervals I=[I−,I+]I=[I^{-},I^{+}]. Each floating-point operation is enlarged outward. If rdn\operatorname{rdn} and rup\operatorname{rup} denote rounding to the adjacent representable number in the downward and upward directions, then

[a,b]+[c,d]=[rdn⁡(a+c),rup⁡(b+d)],[a,b]+[c,d]=[\operatorname{rdn}(a+c),\operatorname{rup}(b+d)],
[a,b]−[c,d]=[rdn⁡(a−d),rup⁡(b−c)],[a,b]-[c,d]=[\operatorname{rdn}(a-d),\operatorname{rup}(b-c)],

and multiplication is the outward-rounded minimum and maximum of the four endpoint products. Division is used only after the denominator interval has been proved not to contain zero. By induction on the arithmetic expression, every interval produced in this manner contains the corresponding exact real quantity.

No transcendental library call is needed for the integer logarithms appearing in the arithmetic sweeps. For 0≤z<10\leq z<1 and R≥1R\geq 1,

Taking z=1/3z=1/3 gives an enclosure of log⁡2\log 2. For an integer x≥2x\geq 2, choose ee with 2e≤x<2e+12^{e}\leq x<2^{e+1} and set

Then

log⁡x=e​log⁡2+2​∑r=0R−1zx2​r+12​r+1+ℛR​(zx).\log x=e\log 2+2\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}\frac{z_{x}^{2r+1}}{2r+1}+\mathcal{R}_{R}(z_{x}). (216)

A.4 Finite arithmetic sweep for AWGC

For a prime power q=pℓq=p^{\ell} put

λq=log⁡p,aq=λq2q.\lambda_{q}=\log p,\qquad a_{q}=\frac{\lambda_{q}^{2}}{q}.

For a bin ℬ\mathcal{B} store

A=∑q∈ℬaq,B=∑q∈ℬλq,C=∑q∈ℬq.A=\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}}a_{q},\qquad B=\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}}\lambda_{q},\qquad C=\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}}q.

Its exact variance contribution is

V⁡(ℬ)=A−B2C,V(\mathcal{B})=A-\frac{B^{2}}{C}, (218)

with V=0V=0 for an empty bin. Cauchy–Schwarz makes (218) non-negative.

Passing from kk to k+1k+1 requires only the following exact updates:

  1. (i)

    add each prime power q|kq\mid k to the bin m=k/qm=k/q in which it becomes active;

  2. (ii)

    remove each prime power q|(k+1)q\mid(k+1), q<k+1q<k+1, from the bin m=(k+1)/q−1m=(k+1)/q-1 in which it ceases to be active;

  3. (iii)

    update ∑mVk,m\sum_{m}V_{k,m} by subtracting the old variance of each changed bin and adding the new variance;

    form σ~k\widetilde{\sigma}_{k} from the prefix of prime powers q<kq<k and remove the prime-power divisors of kk;

  5. (v)

    σ~k−1log⁡2​∑mVk,m\widetilde{\sigma}_{k}-\frac{1}{\log 2}\sum_{m}V_{k,m}

    using only the interval operations above and (216).

Πk=𝖺k−rk∗​𝖣k−1​rk,zk=αk−rk∗​𝖣k−1​vk,δkQ=δk−2​vk∗​𝖣k−1​vk,\Pi_{k}=\mathsf{a}_{k}-r_{k}^{*}\mathsf{D}_{k}^{-1}r_{k},\qquad z_{k}=\alpha_{k}-r_{k}^{*}\mathsf{D}_{k}^{-1}v_{k},\qquad\delta_{k}^{Q}=\delta_{k}-2v_{k}^{*}\mathsf{D}_{k}^{-1}v_{k},

Epilogue: beyond the third gate

The third gate opened without a sound.

Marc, the Arcane Rogue, put away the lockpick. Johnny Nash closed the ledger of loads and pivots only after checking the last dependency once more. Pierre de Fermat inspected the final line and found, this time, enough room in the margin. Mr. Fayman folded the mechanism diagram. Dama Noether lowered her staff; the symmetries had done what the argument asked of them, and nothing more.

Beyond the gate the Critical Strip narrowed, on the party’s map, toward a single luminous line. At the far end of the path stood Princess Clay-la. No one in the party presumed to speak for the reader.

Herr G.F.B.R. left the rulebook open and slid it across the table.

“The map is now the reader’s,” he said.
